question: What category-to-consequence policy should ClawHub adopt for spam or low-quality catalogs, crypto/blockchain/finance/trade content, malicious scan outcomes, and positive trust signals?
rationale: The remaining work decides marketplace trust boundaries and enforcement consequences, which automation should not choose without maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Synthesize Into Public Policy
options.body: Add allowed, not-allowed, edge-case, and consequence guidance to public docs while preserving scanner thresholds and operational tactics in specs.

options.title: Split Into Narrow RFCs
options.body: Use this issue as an umbrella and resolve crypto/wallet, trust-signal, scanner, and quality buckets through narrower linked RFCs before changing docs.

options.title: Keep Case-By-Case For Now
options.body: Leave public policy broad and continue handling these categories through moderator judgment until maintainers are ready to codify them.

recommendation.title: Synthesize Into Public Policy
recommendation.body: Add allowed, not-allowed, edge-case, and consequence guidance to public docs while preserving scanner thresholds and operational tactics in specs.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick authored the RFC and owns the most relevant policy, docs, and moderation scanner history.
